title: Benchmarking News Recommendation in the Era of Green AI
authors: Qijiong Liu, Jieming Zhu, Quanyu Dai, Xiao-Ming Wu
text:
News recommender systems have become a crucial tool in the digital age, helping users discover relevant news articles and stay informed amidst the ever-increasing number of sources available. To integrate news content knowledge into recommender systems, content encoders are employed to capture semantic news representations. Various approaches have been explored in these efforts, including simple content encoders represented by CNN [1] and Attention-based [2] models [3,4,5,6], as well as emerging content encoders based on pretrained language models [7,8].

Despite the success achieved by these studies, there is still a notable absence of standardized benchmarks and uniform evaluation protocols for news recommendation. Consequently, even when common datasets like MIND [9] are employed for evaluation, existing studies often use their own data partitions and apply unique preprocessing steps. The absence of uniformity in data preprocessing methods leads to non-reproducible and often conflicting experimental outcomes across different studies, and the use of non-standard data preprocessing techniques makes it challenging to compare and evaluate results between papers.

Meanwhile, the environmental impact has also begun to draw attention from the machine learning community, as training large-scale networks leads to a huge increase of carbon emission [10]. Therefore, a series of studies [11,12] explore ways to reduce energy consumption in line with Green AI principles [13].

In light of this, we establish the first Green AI Benchmark for News Recommendation, called GreenRec, and introduce a sustainability metric, namely unit conversion rate of carbon emission, to strike a balance between recommendation quality and efficiency. Specifically, we selected six base models and considered five different variants for each model. In total, we evaluated the recommendation accuracy and environmental impact across a total of 30 baselines. This evaluation was carried out under two distinct training paradigms: the conventional end-to-end training paradigm, where the content encoder and other recommender components are jointly trained, and our proposed only-encode-once (OLEO) training paradigm, where the content encoder and other components are trained in a decoupled manner. Our evaluation is conducted through hundreds of experiments within a standardized framework using the most widely used news recommendation datasets, MIND-small and MIND-large [9]. The experiments reveal that the conventional end-to-end paradigm encounters efficiency challenges, while our OLEO-based paradigm is much more eco-friendly. Moreover, the OLEO-based model variants maintain competitive performance with the state-of-the-art end-to-end PLM-NR variants [14], and achieve up to 2992% improvement in our sustainability metric.
